title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Guard GLMGA video sampling against zero source fps
bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

`GLMGAVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` divides by `source.original_fps` in two places — the duration fallback (`round(max_frame_idx / original_fps) + 1`) and `duration_per_frame = 1 / original_fps` — without validating it. vLLM reports `original_fps == 0` for clips with an unknown or variable frame rate (VFR, malformed containers, failed webcam captures), so those inputs crash with a bare `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`.

Every other fps-driven backend in `vllm/multimodal/video.py` already guards this (`Qwen2VLVideoBackend`, `Qwen3VLVideoBackend`, `GLM46VVideoBackend`, and `Molmo2VideoBackend` in fps mode); GLMGA is the remaining one without the check.

## Modifications

- Added the same `original_fps <= 0` guard to `GLMGAVideoBackend`, raising a descriptive `ValueError` that names the backend and the cause, mirroring the existing Qwen2-VL / Qwen3-VL behavior.
- Added a regression test covering both crash paths (duration reported vs. duration missing).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_glmga_video_backend_rejects_unknown_source_fps` -> 1 passed.
- On unpatched `main`, the same test fails with `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero` for both `duration=5.0` (at `duration_per_frame = 1 / original_fps`) and `duration=0.0` (at the duration fallback).
- Neighbor sampling tests `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k glm46v`: 12 passed; the single failure (`test_video_processor_from_model_repo[glm46v]`) is an unrelated missing `av` module in my local environment and fails identically on unpatched `main`.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `glmga`, `glmga fps`, and `video original_fps`: nothing covers the GLMGA backend. #53844 fixes the same bug class for `Qwen3VLVideoBackend` only and does not touch GLMGA; this PR is scoped to GLMGA so the two can land independently.

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI assistance (bug identification, patch, and regression test).

title: [Model Loader][Perf] Auto-prefetch VirtioFS checkpoints
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Enable RAM-guarded safetensors auto-prefetch when the checkpoint filesystem is reported as `virtiofs`.

The default loading mode currently detects `VIRTIOFS` but leaves prefetch disabled because the automatic allowlist contains only NFS, NFS4, and Lustre. With a 1403.19 GiB GLM-5.2 checkpoint that fit within available RAM, explicit prefetch reduced model loading from 1597.0 seconds to 70.7 seconds, about 22.6x.

This change:

- adds VirtioFS to the existing automatic prefetch set;
- renames the internal network-filesystem classification because VirtioFS is a host/guest shared filesystem, not a network filesystem;
- documents default and explicit-lazy behavior;
- adds behavior coverage for VirtioFS, the RAM guard, explicit `lazy`, and a local filesystem.

### Safety and scope

Automatic prefetch still activates only when `safetensors_load_strategy` is unset and total checkpoint size is at most 90% of available RAM. Explicit `lazy` remains an opt-out.

VirtioFS backing storage, cache policy, and DAX configuration vary. The filesystem type alone does not prove that storage is high latency or that prefetched guest pages will be retained. 

This changes startup I/O scheduling only. Loaded tensor values and model outputs are unchanged.

### Duplicate check

Exact VirtioFS issue and PR searches returned no results. #47412 proposes CephFS support through the same mechanism, but only for the separate `ceph` filesystem type. This PR does not include CephFS and can rebase around #47412 if it lands first.

bodyExcerpt:

Add a ModelOpt NVFP4 MegaMoE path backed by DeepGEMM, including fused BF16 shared-expert execution.

- Quantize NVFP4 activations and stage activation/scales/top-k directly into the symmetric buffer in one Triton launch.
- Transform routed NVFP4 weights/scales into the DeepGEMM layout.
- Fuse compatible BF16 shared experts; keep the ordinary shared path for unsupported modules.
- Keep symmetric-buffer allocation/rendezvous outside forward and CUDA Graph capture.
- Fail closed for unsupported router semantics, dtype, bias, LoRA, alignment, platform, DBO, or missing DeepGEMM APIs.
- Preserve the existing ModelOpt path unless `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` is selected.

- Replaced `scaled_fp4_quant` plus temporary tensors and four `copy_` calls with direct-to-symmetric-buffer NVFP4 staging.

## Purpose

#49964 gated the DCP scaling of a group's token span on `isinstance(group.kv_cache_spec, AttentionSpec)` so that Mamba groups stay unscaled. `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is a container rather than an `AttentionSpec` subclass, so DSA models — whose indexer and MLA layers merge into a single uniform group — lost the DCP factor too:

Models whose attention layers share one KV cache group behind `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` — MLA plus its DSA indexer cache (GLM-5.2/GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2-style) — were refused by the canonical portability gate: the wrapper is not an `AttentionSpec`, so `spec_certifiable` returned `False` for the whole group and those models never got a topology-free storage namespace.

title: [Bugfix] glm47 tool parser: tolerate missing opening <arg_value> tag
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #49248.

GLM-4.7-family models sporadically drop the opening `<arg_value>` tag under concurrent load while the argument value and the closing `</arg_value>` tag stay intact:

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key>how many vacation days left</arg_value></tool_call>
```

`_ARG_RE` / `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` in `vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py` required the opening tag, so such recoverable calls silently parsed to `arguments: "{}"`. The client then fails tool-schema validation, the broken `{}` call gets rendered back into chat history, and the agent loop degrades.

This makes the opening `<arg_value>` optional (`(?:<arg_value>)?`) in both regexes. The closing `</arg_value>` still delimits the value, so:
- **Well-formed output is byte-identical** (the optional group matches the tag when present).
- The malformed-but-recoverable call now yields the intended arguments instead of `{}`.
- **Streaming stays monotonic** — an early empty value only advances the safe prefix to the open quote (`{"city": "`), which is a clean prefix of the later `{"city": "Beijing"}` under the engine's `_safe_arg_prefix` diff logic, so no delta corruption.

The model-side token skip is a model quirk vLLM cannot prevent, but the parser turning a fully recoverable call into `{}` with no diagnostic makes it much worse than it needs to be.

## Test Plan

Added regression tests in `tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py`:
- `test_missing_opening_arg_value_tag` (non-streaming)
- `test_missing_opening_arg_value_tag_with_newline` (structural whitespace stripped)
- `test_missing_opening_arg_value_tag_multiple_args` (malformed + well-formed args mixed)
- `test_missing_opening_arg_value_tag` (streaming counterpart)

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_glm47_moe_tool_parser.py

title: [Bugfix][MiniCPM-V] Route video_embeds to the shared vision parser
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

MiniCPM-V routes video inputs through the image vision parser, stripping the `video_`
prefix off its multi-modal kwargs on the way:

```python
self._parse_and_validate_vision_input(
    "videos", **{k.removeprefix("video_"): v for k, v in kwargs.items()}
)
```

That works for `video_pixel_values` and `video_tgt_sizes`. It does not work for
`video_embeds`, because the image field is named `image_embeds`, not `embeds`. The
parser pops `image_embeds`, never sees the renamed key, and behaves as if no video
were passed.

`video_embeds` is a declared multi-modal field on both models, in
`_minicpmv_field_config` and `_minicpmv4_6_field_config`. It can be passed offline
through `multi_modal_data`, and #54242 added the chat frontend path for
`video_embeds` content parts, both under `--enable-mm-embeds`. Users hit this in
two ways. On 2.6 the parser returns `None`, which is stored as
`modalities["videos"]` and then subscripted by `_process_vision_input`, raising
`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. On 4.6 the guard reads
`video_kwargs.get("image_embeds")`, which is absent after the rename, so the video
branch is skipped and the video is dropped with no error at all.

Other VLMs give video its own `_parse_and_validate_video_input` that pops
`video_embeds` by name, Qwen2.5-VL and GLM-4.1V among them. MiniCPM-V shares the
image parser on purpose, since its videos run the same vision pipeline, so this
keeps that structure and replaces the prefix strip with an explicit video-to-image
kwarg mapping used by both models.

Restricting the mapping to video keys also stops image kwargs reaching the video
parser. The old comprehension rewrote every kwarg, so an `image_embeds` sent in the
same request was passed through to the video call untouched.

title: [XPU][Bugfix] Defer Inductor compile-time autotuning to avoid fatal profile_run abort
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

On Intel XPU, serving a model with `torch.compile` enabled (the default `VLLM_COMPILE` path) can abort during startup's `profile_run()` -> `_dummy_run()` -> AOT `standalone_compile`, with an opaque, contentless error:

```
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: RuntimeError: Failed to run autotuning code block:
```

Root cause (filed upstream: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194018): Inductor's compile-time autotuning (`triton.autotune_at_compile_time`, enabled by default whenever `V.aot_compilation` is set -- which is exactly the path `vllm/compilation/wrapper.py`'s `aot_compile()` uses during `profile_run`) benchmarks each generated Triton kernel once at compile time using synthetic random inputs (`torch._dynamo.testing.rand_strided`). Kernels whose index is derived from floating-point intermediate data (RoPE/MLA position or offset arithmetic is a common pattern in MLA architectures such as DeepSeek-V2/V3/GLM) get a genuinely randomized index at that point, which can be out of range and trip the `tl.device_assert` bounds check Inductor emits for indirect indexing (`assert_indirect_indexing=True` by default). On CPU/CUDA this is generally recoverable; on XPU a failed device-side assert is fatal to the Level-Zero driver context, killing the whole worker process and surfacing only the opaque message above.

This is not an XPU-only codegen bug -- the graph/codegen path is identical across backends -- but XPU's fatal handling of the underlying device fault makes it the only backend where this currently surfaces as a hard crash. A proper fix belongs in PyTorch Inductor (clamp/mask the synthesized index tensors, or relax the assert during the autotune-benchmarking exec block); this PR is the vLLM-side mitigation until that lands upstream.

**Fix**: default `triton.autotune_at_compile_time` to `False` on XPU whenever compilation is enabled, in `XPUPlatform.check_and_update_config`, following the same `inductor_compile_config.setdefault(...)`

title: [Bug]: step3p5 parser bypasses XML parsing for named/required tool_choice
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

The built-in `Step3p5ToolParser` emits valid OpenAI tool calls for `tool_choice: "auto"`, but named/required tool choices bypass its XML parser because the class inherits `ToolParser.supports_required_and_named = True`. The Step 3.5/3.7 format is XML, so the serving layer incorrectly wraps the raw XML as `function.arguments` instead of invoking `extract_tool_calls`.

Current `main` still lacks the override. XML-based parsers such as `Glm47MoeModelToolParser` correctly set `supports_required_and_named = False`.

## Environment

- Official StepFun image: `vllm/vllm-openai:stepfun37@sha256:17fae7886712d62b4c19f98481fd86dcde78fae89162200fd4e462c215de8db3`
- vLLM: `0.1.dev16944+ge9c8946e7`
- Model: `stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash-FP8@b3d7916fccac844cca050d7520f2aaa513f9a84f`
- Server flags include the publisher-recommended `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser step3p5 --reasoning-parser step3p5`

## Reproducer

Send a chat completion with one function and:

```json
"tool_choice": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "report_sum"}}
```

The model generates:

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=report_sum>
<parameter=a>3</parameter>
<parameter=b>4</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

Observed OpenAI response excerpt:

```json
{"function":{"name":"report_sum","arguments":"<tool_call>\n<function=report_sum>..."},"type":"function"}
```

With `tool_choice: "auto"`, the same request is parsed correctly as `arguments: "{\"a\": 3, \"b\": 4}"`. Streaming auto tool calls also parse correctly.

## Root cause

`OpenAIServing._parse_tool_calls_from_content` uses the standard JSON branch for named/required choices when `tool_parser_cls.supports_required_and_named` is true. `Step3p5ToolParser` parses XML but does not override the inherited true value, so `extract_tool_calls` is skipped.

## Expected fix

Add this class property and generic parser coverage for named and required choices:

```python
class Step3p5ToolParser(ToolParser):

title: [bug]: empty JSON schema `{}` causes unbounded number death-loop garbled output
bodyExcerpt:
# Empty JSON schema `{}` causes unbounded number death-loop garbled output

## Summary

When a structured-output request uses an empty JSON schema `{"json": {}}` (equivalent to "accept any JSON value"), vLLM compiles it into a grammar whose `number` branch is unbounded and cannot be terminated. The model falls into a number death-loop, emitting up to `max_tokens` of pure digits (a single giant valid JSON number), instead of a normal JSON value. `reasoning_content` (thinking phase) is unaffected — only the final `content` is garbled.

This reproduces on **GPU** as well as Ascend NPU (confirmed by a colleague on GPU vLLM; sglang does **not** reproduce). So it is a vLLM upstream issue, not backend/platform-specific.

## Environment

- vLLM version: `v0.20.3.dev47+g8d52ba3cd` (branch `hpu-release/release-v0.20.2-20260601`, commit `8d52ba3cd`)
- Model: GLM-5.1 (w8a8), with `--reasoning-parser glm45` (thinking enabled)
- Backend: structured_outputs `auto` (resolves to `guidance`/`llguidance`; also reproduces with `xgrammar`/`outlines`)
- Hardware: Ascend HPU 910A3 (also reproduced on GPU)
- Deployment: prefill-decode disaggregation (pd-sep) — but the bug is not pd-sep-specific; it is in the structured-output schema compilation path

## Reproduction

### Request

```bash
curl -s http://<endpoint>/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "auto",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "你好"}],
    "structured_outputs": {"json": {}},
    "stream": false,
    "max_tokens": 51200
  }'
```

The key trigger is `structured_outputs: {"json": {}}` — an **empty JSON schema dict**. In JSON Schema semantics, `{}` (no `type` keyword) means "accept any JSON value" (object/array/string/number/boolean/null).

### Actual (buggy) result

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "1.1478652e-0852808689391498581278959278115265275173994480839003085814898587224337225458316874850289548247142149196596559984
author: MarinaMiao

title: [Bug]: V2 sampler warmup misses explicit-seed native path when FlashInfer is enabled
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Field deployment:

- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs (97,887 MiB each)
- NVIDIA driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2
- TP4 / DCP4, V2 model runner, FlashInfer sampler enabled
- Full GLM-5.3 checkpoint on a downstream vLLM/B12X image

The fatal field reproduction was on a downstream build, not stock vLLM `main`. I am filing this upstream because the same dispatch invariant is present in upstream commit [`5e71a11e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

V2 sampler warmup does not exercise the native sampling path selected by an explicit per-request seed when FlashInfer is enabled. Consequently, the engine can become ready before native top-k/top-p and Gumbel kernels have compiled or made their first temporary allocations. The first seeded API request can then JIT/allocate a materially different path and OOM under tight residual headroom.

The source path at `5e71a11e` is deterministic:

1. [`SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/sampling_params.py#L1234-L1253) says it exercises all sampler logic, but supplies no `seed`.
2. [`warmup_kernels()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/warmup.py#L257-L283) assigns that unseeded configuration to all warmup requests.
3. The V2 sampler [disables FlashInfer when `any_explicit_seed()` is true](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede15ecc39c7dddca38e03deb5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py#L284-L320). With no seed, warmup takes FlashInfer; a seeded request takes native top-k/top-p plus Gumbel.
4. Although current warmup includes a one-request decode step, it remains unseeded. If the native path were selected, a batch below eight rows would [use the PyTorch full-vocabulary sort path](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5e71a11eb2b595ede1

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize null assistant content with tool_calls
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- Normalize assistant messages with `content: null` and `tool_calls` to use an empty string before chat templating.
- Prevents Jinja templates that render `{{ content }}` from injecting the literal string `None` into the prompt.
- Adds regression coverage in `test_chat_utils.py`.

## Problem

OpenAI agent clients (OpenAI SDK, pi, etc.) commonly send assistant turns as `content: null` plus `tool_calls`. When those messages reach `apply_chat_template`, templates that unconditionally render assistant content emit `None` as text. Over many tool-calling turns in an agent session, this silently degrades generation into repetition loops and looks like a model quality issue rather than a preprocessing bug.

Reported in #54337 with reproduction on GLM chat templates; the fix is protocol-layer and model-agnostic.

## Fix

Extend `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` to coerce `content=None` to `""` for assistant messages that include `tool_calls`, alongside the existing tool-call argument normalization.

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke-tested `_postprocess_messages` locally (null content becomes `""`, arguments still parsed)
- [ ] `pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_null_content_with_tool_calls -q`
- [ ] `pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py::test_postprocess_messages_null_arguments_string -q`

Fixes #54337

title: [KV offload] Scale uniform-type attention groups by DCP in build_offloading_config
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` scales a KV-cache group's `tokens_per_block` by `decode_context_parallel_size` only when the group spec is a bare `AttentionSpec`. Models whose attention layers are merged into one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group (GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek-V3.2: MLA layers plus the sparse-indexer K cache) are block-sharded across DCP ranks exactly like a plain attention group but skipped the multiplier. Under DCP the hash block size from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` is `block_size * dcp`, so the `OffloadingConnector` failed at startup:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=64 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=512. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

(GLM-5.2-FP8 prefill, `--decode-context-parallel-size 8`, `MultiConnector` = NixlConnector + OffloadingConnector/`TieringOffloadingSpec`.)

Fix: treat a group as DCP-sharded when every layer spec it covers is an `AttentionSpec` (via `iter_layer_specs`). Mamba groups keep their full per-rank block as before, and the result matches how the scheduler block size is resolved.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_dcp_scales_uniform_type_attention_group_blocks` (uniform group of two MLA specs, DCP=2 → `tokens_per_block == tokens_per_hash == 32`).
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -k "dcp or prefill_context"` → 4 passed.
- E2E: GLM-5.2-FP8 PCP8×DCP8 prefill with NIXL + CPU offloading now starts (previously asserted at connector init).

## Test Result

Unit tests pass; E2E deployment starts with offloading enabled under DCP8.

title: [Bug][Core] --enable-dbo forces the V1 model runner, making dual batch overlap unreachable for every DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES model (and killing startup for GLM-5.3-Flash)
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

`--enable-dbo` forces the V1 model runner. Architectures listed in
`DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES` therefore cannot use dual batch overlap — and
those are exactly the large MoE models for which expert parallelism, and hence DBO, is
most valuable.

```
WARNING [vllm.py:693] Model Runner V2 does not yet support dual batch overlap;
                      using the V1 model runner instead.
```

For `Glm5NextForCausalLM` the fallback does not merely lose V2 features, it does not
start: the server produces 19 log lines and exits without a traceback.

### Why this matters, with measurements

On 8×MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2.3) serving a self-quantized MXFP4 `GLM-5.3-Flash`,
expert parallelism loses badly to plain replication — three runs per point:

| concurrency | TP1 × 8 replicas | DP8+EP8, `allgather_reducescatter` | DP8+EP8, `mori_high_throughput` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 192 | 6 140 tok/s | 4 423 ±37 (−28.0 %) | 3 802 ±65 (−38.1 %) |
| 256 | 6 992 tok/s | 4 990 ±23 (−28.6 %) | 4 298 ±43 (−38.5 %) |

The memory incentive for EP is real: each GPU holds 36 of 288 experts (~21 GB instead
of 166 GB) and sees ~21 tokens per expert instead of 2.7, which also fixes the small-M
GEMM problem. It loses anyway because of the **number of synchronizing collectives**:
two all-to-all rounds per MoE layer × 42 layers = 84 per forward pass.

That this is a synchronization cost and not a bandwidth cost is confirmed by the
cross-test above — `allgather_reducescatter` moves *more* data with *fewer, simpler*
collectives and is consistently 16 % faster than MoRI.

Hiding that latency behind computation is exactly what DBO does (and what SGLang's
TBO/SBO do). It is the one remaining lever that could make EP competitive here, and it
is unreachable for this model class.

### Repro

```bash
vllm serve <glm-5.3-flash-mxfp4> \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --enable-dbo \
  --quantization quar

title: [ROCm] Fused shared experts unavailable for GLM-5.3-Flash: Fp8Config not handled by the FSE gate, and glm5next never wires it
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash has `n_shared_experts = 1`, but AITER fused shared experts (FSE) cannot be used with it for two independent reasons. The first is a one-line gate I have a working patch for; the second is model wiring that needs an MTP-aware decision.

### 1. `Fp8Config` is not handled by the FSE compatibility gate

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` (`model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/config_utils.py`) special-cases `DeepseekV4FP8Config` and `QuarkConfig`, then falls through to:

```
shared-expert FSE quantization compatibility is not implemented for Fp8Config
```

For a plain fp8 checkpoint this looks safe to allow. `Fp8Config` applies one global `weight_block_size` and one activation scheme to everything it covers, so the routed and shared experts carry the same scheme by construction — the only way they can diverge is if exactly one side sits in `ignored_layers`. GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8 has `weight_block_size: [128, 128]`, `activation_scheme: dynamic`, `ignored_layers: null`.

```python
    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.fp8 import Fp8Config

    if isinstance(quant_config, Fp8Config):
        from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
            is_layer_skipped,
        )

        ignored = quant_config.ignored_layers or []
        experts_skipped = is_layer_skipped(expert_prefix, ignored, match_mode="suffix")
        shared_skipped = is_layer_skipped(
            shared_expert_prefix, ignored, match_mode="suffix"
        )
        if experts_skipped != shared_skipped:
            side = shared_expert_prefix if shared_skipped else expert_prefix
            return False, (
                f"fp8 quantization covers only one side of the fusion ({side} "
                "is in ignored_layers)"
            )
        return True, None
```

With this the gate opens and the warning disappears. Happy to send it as a PR on its own if you want it independent of the rest.

title: [Bug][Quantization] Quark MXFP4 checkpoints are unloadable for multimodal models: exclude list is in checkpoint naming while vLLM matches module naming (plus 4 related name-granularity mismatches)
bodyExcerpt:
### Quark MXFP4 checkpoints are unusable for any model whose loader renames prefixes (all multimodal ones)

Producing an MXFP4 checkpoint of `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` with AMD Quark 0.12
(`quantize_model_per_safetensor`, the recipe from the `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` model card)
yields weights that are byte-for-byte the right format but that vLLM cannot load.
Two independent causes, both invisible on a text-only model:

**1. The `exclude` list is written in checkpoint naming; vLLM matches module naming.**

Quark expands the `--exclude_layers` globs against *checkpoint tensor names* and stores
the expansion in `config.json`. vLLM's `is_layer_skipped` compares against *module
prefixes* with `match_mode="exact"`. For a text-only model these are the same string,
so `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` works. GLM-5.3-Flash is multimodal, and its loader applies

```
"model.language_model." -> "language_model.model."
"model.visual."         -> "visual."
"lm_head."              -> "language_model.lm_head."
```

so **not one** of the 1550 exclude entries matches. Every excluded layer is then built
quantized, and loading the bf16 weights Quark wrote for them fails:

```
[MODUL] language_model.model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj shard=0
        param_voll=(12288, 2048)/torch.uint8
        geladen=(12288, 4096)/torch.bfloat16
        quant_method=QuarkLinearMethod
```

This affects *every* multimodal architecture, not just GLM.

**2. vLLM queries the exclude list under fused module names; Quark only lists the parts.**

`glm5next` fuses `gate_proj`+`up_proj` into `gate_up_proj`, `q_a_proj`+
`kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into `fused_qkv_a_proj`, `wk`+`weights_proj` into
`wk_weights_proj`, and six KDA projections into `in_proj_qkvbfg_a`. The exclude list
contains only the constituents. `is_layer_skipped` has a `fused_mapping` parameter for
exactly this, but the model defines **no `packed_modules_mapping`**, so nothing
resolves the fused name back to its parts.

title: [Kernel] Default unquantized BF16 linear to FlashInfer mm_bf16 and drop the CuTe skinny GEMM
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Make FlashInfer `mm_bf16` with `backend="auto"` the **default** GEMM for unquantized
BF16 linear layers, and remove the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM it supersedes.

`default_unquantized_gemm` currently always calls `torch.nn.functional.linear`, so
every BF16 dense projection and the LM head land on cuBLAS regardless of shape.
Routing through `mm_bf16(..., backend="auto")` lets FlashInfer pick among
cuDNN / CUTLASS / TGV / cuBLASLt / TinyGEMM per shape. Related:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27173,
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35467

Once that is the default, the hand-tuned CuTe skinny GEMM
(`model_executor/kernels/linear/cute_dsl/skinny_gemm.py`) and its per-shape config
tables in the Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.2 low-latency selectors are redundant, so the second
commit deletes them and reduces both tables to the `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` entries they
still need. Shapes that were CuTe-only now fall through to the default path.

The two commits are separable — if reviewers want the default switch on its own,
the second commit can be dropped.

### Relationship to existing PRs

Both existing FlashInfer BF16 PRs add an **opt-in** backend and leave the default
path on `torch.nn.functional.linear`. This PR changes the default. That is the
material difference, and it is also the part most worth arguing about.

- **#40638** (@raayandhar) is the closest overlap: it also calls `mm_bf16` with
  `backend="auto"`, but behind a new `--bf16-linear-backend` flag that defaults to

  collaboration on the integration. If maintainers prefer that shape, I am happy to

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix BLHNC addressing for FlashInfer sparse MLA
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix sparse MLA cache addressing when `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` uses a block-outermost KV-cache layout such as BLHNC.

BLHNC places other layers' pages between consecutive blocks of a given layer. Two paths incorrectly assumed that a layer's physical block stride was exactly its logical block size:

- FlashInfer sparse index conversion multiplied the physical block ID by `block_size`, causing decode to read another layer's page.
- The fused DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM cache writer derived the logical block size from the physical block stride, causing writes to land in the wrong block or layer.

## Changes

- Derive the physical row stride from the actual FlashInfer KV-cache view and pass it through both regular and DCP sparse-index conversion.
- Pass the logical MLA block size explicitly to the fused cache writer.
- Extend DCP physical-remapping coverage to a non-dense block stride.

gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "BLHNC"

title: [Bug][Feature][KV-offloading]: shared-mmap CPU region assumes all ranks on one host — multi-node engines hang at init; node-local disk tier reference implementation
bodyExcerpt:
### Bug half

`SharedOffloadRegion` is one mmap file with a slot per rank. On a multi-node engine (mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, ranks on different hosts) the remote rank's slot is never written and startup dies after a multi-minute opaque wait:

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for mmap file to reach 4144029696 bytes
```

`TieringOffloadingSpec` cannot avoid it: it overrides `_uses_shared_region → True` because the scheduler-side StoreController pushes L1 bytes to secondary tiers through a whole-region memoryview — single-host by construction. Plain `CPUOffloadingSpec` could fall back to private pinned tensors (which work fine multi-node), but has no gate either.

**Suggested minimal fix:** detect ranks-per-host at spec init and fail fast with an explicit "multi-node engines are not supported by the shared-region CPU tier" (or fall back to private tensors for the non-tiering spec). Related lifecycle work: #51317 / #52596 (leaked/unlinked regions — we added supporting evidence there from unified-memory hardware, where leaked regions silently shrink the next boot's profiled memory).

### Feature half: node-local tier for multi-node engines

For multi-node engines we built a working alternative worth considering in-tree: a spec where the scheduler keeps **metadata only** (persistent key index; per-key file paths derived from block hashes) and **each rank performs its own disk I/O against node-local storage** — shards never cross nodes and are never duplicated. ~450 lines over `CPUOffloadingSpec`, loaded via the existing `spec_module_path` hook, no core changes beyond the per-group geometry in #54413.

Production numbers (2× NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10 unified memory, GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 TP=2 with DFlash2 speculation): 155k-token session restored in 36.6 s vs 205 s recompute after a **full engine restart**; 10 *simultaneous* restores after restart, 10/10 needle-correct, TTFTs 18–164 s stacking gracefully.

title: [Feature][KV-offloading]: recent-window state groups can never participate in restores — per-group offload exclusion + hit-boundary rollback (GLM-5.3 tail_cache)
bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Some hybrid-model KV groups hold *recent-window state* rather than restorable prefix state. GLM-5.3-Flash's 4-token DSA-indexer `tail_cache` keeps only a live window, which breaks the OffloadingConnector three independent ways:

1. Its engine-side block table is much shorter than `cdiv(hit_tokens, block_size)`, so `update_state_after_alloc` dies on `assert len(group_blocks) >= num_gpu_blocks` for any external hit that includes the group.
2. SWA-style store selection always lands on null placeholder blocks — the group can never store a chunk.
3. Any lookup chain that includes it collapses the min-across-groups hit window to zero — so one such group makes the **whole model** un-restorable even when every other group's chunks are stored and hit.

Related: #52771 / #52735 diagnose the adjacent all-groups-drafter-fallback defect under MTP/EAGLE (which we also hit); this issue is about groups that are *architecturally* unrestorable rather than volatile-tail handling.

### Proposed change (running in production)

Three cooperating hooks (config-driven in our deployment, `kv_connector_extra_config`):

- `load_skip_groups`: the group contributes an empty entry to load specs (workers already skip zero-size groups), so its short block table never trips the allocation assert;
- manager-level **always-hit / never-store** for those groups, so they neither gate nor pollute the hit window;
- `hit_rollback_tokens`: report one mamba-align segment (3,584 tokens here) fewer hit tokens, so the engine **recomputes** the trailing segment — which honestly rebuilds tail/conv/drafter state from the restored KV. title: [Feature][KV-offloading]: OffloadingConnector rejects hybrid models whose KV groups have blocks smaller than one hash unit (GLM-5.3-Flash) — per-group blocks_per_chunk implementation attached
bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`build_offloading_config` asserts `tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0` for every KV cache group, so a hybrid model with any group whose blocks are *smaller* than a hash unit cannot enable the OffloadingConnector at all. GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, TP=2) is such a model — its DSA-indexer `tail_cache` group has **4-token blocks** under a 64-token hash grid. Boot-time group inventory from our deployment:

```
group[0]   UniformType 3584 tok  (MLA + indexer k_cache, 22 layers)
group[1]   UniformType    4 tok  (indexer tail_cache, 11 layers)   <- rejected
group[2-5] MambaSpec   3584 tok  (KDA state, align mode)
group[6]   UniformType   64 tok  (DFlash2 drafter)
tokens_per_hash = 64
```

This is the same disease family as #48635 (block_size uniformity, completed) and #48919 (eagle-group block-size mismatch, open): group geometry threaded through the stack as a single global scalar. #38261 attacks the same problem with a planner that splits groups, and #44865 reshapes transfer descriptors per-group — this issue offers a third, minimal-footprint approach plus a production data point, in the hope of converging on one design.

### Proposed change (running in production)

Support the divisor direction: a group with `tokens_per_hash % tokens_per_block == 0` aggregates `tokens_per_hash // tokens_per_block` GPU blocks per offloaded chunk. Concretely, `blocks_per_chunk` becomes **per-group** — derived on `OffloadingSpec`, carried on `GroupOffloadConfig`, and substituted at the scheduler sites that read the global scalar (`storable_chunks`, `update_state_after_alloc`, `_update_req_states`, `_build_store_jobs`, `resolve_mamba_align_size`, the `from_spec` geometry). `GPULoadStoreSpec.block_indices` already anticipates offload-units larger than GPU blocks.

One practical note: keeping the CPU staging tier **row-granular** (worker at bpc=1, manager allocating `bpc[g]` rows per key) sidesteps tensors shared between gr

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Read the DFlash target's RoPE layout from an attention's own rotary_emb
bodyExcerpt:
### Purpose

`dflash_target_rope_is_neox_style` walks the target's modules and returns the
first `is_neox_style` it finds. On a NoPE target that is not the attention's
rope — it is whatever other rope the model happens to build.

GLM-5.3-Flash (#53906) is the concrete case. Its MLA attention sets
`self.rotary_emb = None` under `mla_nope`, but the sparse indexer beside it
builds `indexer_rope_emb = ...(is_neox_style=not config.indexer_rope_interleave)`.
The walk finds the indexer's rope and reports `False`, so the DFlash head is
forced to non-neox against its Qwen3 default of `True`. Nothing errors and the
output stays correct — acceptance just collapses to 1.0.

The vision tower is a second instance of the same hazard: it declares
`is_neox_style=True`, and which one the walk reaches first is incidental.

### Why no existing target hits this

Before #51655 the draft did not consult the target at all — it took the Qwen3
default from `getattr(config, "is_neox_style", True)`, which is correct for
every neox target DFlash supported. #51655 added the probe for targets with
interleaved RoPE, and on those the walk is right: their attention has a real
rope, so the first `is_neox_style` a pre-order walk reaches is the attention's.

The failure needs a target whose attention has *no* rope while the model builds
one elsewhere. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first such target.

### Fix

Read the layout off a module's own `rotary_emb` rather than off any module that
declares `is_neox_style`. A NoPE attention holds `rotary_emb = None`, which is
not a layout, so the walk runs to the end and returns `None` — the draft then
keeps the layout it was distilled with.

```diff
-        style = getattr(module, "is_neox_style", None)
+        style = getattr(getattr(module, "rotary_emb", None), "is_neox_style", None)
```

Inside `get_language_model()` every rope in the tree is named `rotary_emb` (89
sites); the two other names, `rotary_pos_emb` and `rotary_embedding`, belong to
vision and audio encod

title: [Bug]: Assistant `content=null` + `tool_calls` renders literal "None" into chat template context — degenerate outputs in agent workloads
bodyExcerpt:
### Environment
- vLLM: `v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (also present on recent mainline `dev` builds)
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (any GLM chat template that emits per-turn `<think>` and renders `{{ content }}` for assistant turns; the keys/GLM stock `chat_template.jinja` is affected)
- Hardware: 4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), TP4
- Client: pi agent (any agent harness sending `content: null` + `tool_calls` assistant turns — standard OpenAI agent format; cursor/openai-python do the same)

### Symptom
Long agent sessions (multi-turn tool calling) intermittently produce **degenerate repetitive outputs** (e.g. an infinite loop of `# --` or a single reasoning loop consuming the entire `max_tokens` budget with zero content tokens). Probability increases with the number of tool-call turns in history.

### Root cause
When an agent client sends an assistant message with `content: null` and `tool_calls`, the message passes through to `apply_chat_template` with `content=None`. The GLM chat template renders this turn as:

```
<|assistant|><think></think>None<tool_call>bash<arg_key>...
                       ^^^^ literal "None"
```

Verified with `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` (transformers 4.5x):

```python
msgs = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "check metrics"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [...]},   # agent turn
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "c0", "content": "run=3"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "continue"},
]
tok.apply_chat_template(msgs, tools=tools, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
# → '<|assistant|><think></think>None<tool_call>bash...'
#    with content="" instead of None:
# → '<|assistant|><think></think><tool_call>bash...'   (clean)
```

Every tool-calling turn injects one literal `None` token-sequence into the context. After 8-20 turns (a normal agent session) the model's in-context pattern degrades and reasoning collapses into repetition loops.

title: [Bug]: _compute_slot_mapping_kernel reads block_table out of bounds for cache groups whose block table is narrower than the sequence
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

`_compute_slot_mapping_kernel` in `vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py` masks its block-table load by
token validity and CP ownership, but **not** by whether the computed column index is inside the
row. Any KV cache group whose block table does not span the sequence in raw token positions
therefore performs an unbounded out-of-bounds read, scaling with sequence length.

On 8× MI325X (gfx942, ROCm 7.2.3) this eventually crosses into an unmapped page and takes down
every rank with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N ... Reason: Unknown`.

### The missing guard

`vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py` @ `main` `94d96e24`:

```python
block_indices = (                                    # :463-466
    virtual_block_indices * BLOCKS_PER_KV_BLOCK
    + local_block_offsets // block_size
)
block_numbers = tl.load(                             # :467-471
    block_table_ptr + row_offset + block_indices,
    mask=mask & is_local,                            # :469  ← no range term
    other=0,
).to(tl.int64)
slot_offsets = local_block_offsets % block_size
slot_ids = block_numbers * block_size + slot_offsets
slot_ids = tl.where(is_local, slot_ids, PAD_ID)      # :474  ← no range term
```

The model-side QSA slot helpers in #53896 do bound this (`valid &= logical_blocks < block_table.shape[1]`
and a clamp before indexing); the generic kernel is the one path we found that does not.

### Two independent instances, both from in-flight model PRs

Neither spec class is on `main` yet; both are added by open PRs, and each declares a
**one-block-per-request** side cache that the kernel then indexes with **raw token positions**:

| PR | spec | `max_num_blocks_per_req()` | effective row width | index computed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #53896 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) | `CircularBufferSpec` | `1` | 128 tokens (after the 128-token alignment in `get_block_table_width`) | `pos // 8` |

title: [Hy4] support Hy4-preview model
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview

  cd vllm

  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

title: [ROCm/MoRIIO] fix: guard req_id_to_index lookup for synthetic KV-connector req_ids
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Fixes a `KeyError` in `scheduler.update_from_output` that crashes the EngineCore on the first request in PD-disaggregated mode when using the MoRIIO WideEP KV connector.

## Root cause

MoRIIO routes synthetic health-probe requests with compound req_ids (embedding prefill+decode host:port addresses) through the scheduler. These req_ids appear in `num_scheduled_tokens` but are intentionally absent from `model_runner_output.req_id_to_index`. The unconditional `req_id_to_index[req_id]` lookup raises `KeyError` → `EngineDeadError` on every first inference request.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: Add guard before the index lookup:
  ```python
  if req_id not in model_runner_output.req_id_to_index:
      continue  # synthetic KV-connector req not in output index
  ```
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_kv_connector.py`: Four unit tests (no GPU required, `pytest.mark.cpu_test`):
  - `test_no_keyerror_with_single_synthetic_req_id` — reproduces the crash
  - `test_normal_requests_processed_alongside_synthetic` — regression guard
  - `test_multiple_synthetic_req_ids_skipped` — batch with 5 synthetic IDs
  - `test_purely_synthetic_batch_does_not_crash` — empty model output

## Test plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler_kv_connector.py -v
```

All tests are CPU-only (`pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test`).

## Related

Discovered during GLM-5.2-FP8 WideEP PD-disaggregated serving validation on AMD MI300X (vLLM v0.27.1 + MoRIIO PR#176 overlay, 1P1D / 1P2D / 2P2D EP8/EP16 topologies).

title: [Bug]: Quark FSE compatibility check matches `shared_expert_gate`, silently disabling fused shared experts on Qwen MoE MXFP4
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` decides whether AITER fused shared experts (FSE) may run by searching the **entire** Quark `exclude` list for the substring `shared_expert`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/config_utils.py#L106-L111

```python
is_compatible = not any(
    "shared_expert" in str(entry)
    for entry in quant_config.quant_config["exclude"]
)
if not is_compatible:
    return False, f"Quark excludes shared experts at {shared_expert_prefix}"
```

That substring also matches `mlp.shared_expert_gate`, which is a **different module**: the `hidden_size -> 1` router gate that scales the shared expert's output. It is BF16 by design (quantizing a 1-column projection is pointless), so every Qwen MoE Quark checkpoint lists it in `exclude` — including checkpoints whose shared-expert projections are fully MXFP4.

The result is that FSE is refused on exactly the checkpoints it was enabled for. Nothing fails and accuracy is unchanged; the shared expert simply runs unfused, costing the FSE speedup on ROCm, with only a per-MoE-layer startup warning:

```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS is enabled but cannot be enabled:
Quark excludes shared experts at model.layers.0.mlp.shared_expert.
```

## Regression

Introduced in #51695, which moved Qwen off its own local check onto the shared helper. The previous Qwen check matched `"shared_expert."` **with the trailing dot**, which only matched real projections (`shared_expert.down_proj`) and correctly ignored the `shared_expert_gate` sibling:

```python
# removed in #51695, vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py
return not any("shared_expert." in str(e) for e in exclude)
```

The dot appears to have been dropped so one substring could cover both the Qwen singular `shared_expert.` and the DeepSeek/GLM plural `shared_experts.`. The test added in that PR only exercises the plural naming and never a `shared_expert_gate` sibling, which is why

title: [Attention] Enable dense and masked MHA for GLM-5
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/179.

This PR enables the sparse-MLA masked-MHA prefill path for the GLM-5 256/256 QK/V head dimensions:

- Temporarily pins FlashAttention to `MatthewBonanni/flash-attention@8f844a0`, which contains head-dim-256 `mask_mod` support.
- Admits the GLM-5 dimensions `(64 heads, KV rank 512, QK 192+64, V 256)` to the existing masked-MHA route.
- Keeps the general FA4 head-dim-256 selector disabled. Sparse masked MHA uses contiguous projected K/V, while paged decoder attention still has unsupported non-page-aligned `max_seqlen_k` cases.
- Adds backend-specific GLM-5 routing thresholds derived from masked-MHA-vs-sparse-MQA benchmarks while leaving the existing DeepSeek thresholds unchanged.
- Extends the existing sparse-MLA reference test across DeepSeek 192/128 and GLM-5 256/256 dimensions, including cached context.

No other open PR was found for GLM-5 masked-MHA support.

### Routing policy and workspace guard

The threshold table records the benchmark-derived performance policy, including winning regions above 32K so it remains useful if the workspace limit changes. The existing workspace-capacity check is an independent final guard. With the current fixed 128 MiB workspace, a single pure-prefill request fits at exactly 32K and requests above 32K fall back to sparse MQA even when admitted by the performance policy. Batch size and cached context can make the workspace guard apply earlier.

The measured FlashMLA pure-prefill MHA-to-MQA crossovers were approximately 8.5K, 20.8K, 52.8K, and 116.8K tokens for TP1/2/4/8. The policy uses rounded conservative limits:

| TP | FlashMLA pure-prefill policy limit |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8K |
| 2 | 20K |
| 4 | 48K |
| 8 | 112K |

Cached-context routing uses a separate query/sequence-length table. TP1 stays on MQA when context is present; TP2/4/8 select masked MHA only inside benchmarked winning regions.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Let the reasoning parser decide reasoning_ended when reasoning is hidden
bodyExcerpt:
Ask the configured reasoning parser instead, so structured outputs aren't enforced inside <think> for models that always reason.




## Purpose

`OpenAIServingChat` forces `reasoning_ended=True` for the structured-output gate whenever `include_reasoning=False`, treating "the client doesn't want to see reasoning" as "the model won't produce reasoning". For models whose chat template always opens the assistant turn with `<think>` (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) the block is still generated, so a `json_schema` response format or strict-tool grammar is enforced from the first token, inside the reasoning. Result: ~30 completion tokens, empty `content`, `reasoning_tokens=0`. OpenRouter's `reasoning.exclude` maps to exactly this request shape, so it shows up as broken structured output there.

This PR lets the configured reasoning parser decide (`is_reasoning_end(prompt_token_ids)`) and keeps the `include_reasoning` shortcut only for servers with no reasoning parser. The check keys on the server-level reasoning-parser setting rather than `parser.reasoning_parser`, because when tool and reasoning parsing share one parser engine, `ParserManager.get_parser` returns the engine class itself and that attribute is `None`. Note: this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); the code and tests were reviewed and validated end-to-end by the author.

## Test Plan

Unit test added: `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_reasoning_gate.py` — asserts the `reasoning_ended` value passed to `engine.generate` with an engine-style parser (no `reasoning_parser` attribute) for hidden and visible reasoning, and the legacy shortcut when no reasoning parser is configured.

## Test Result

Before: `finish_reason=stop`, `completion_tokens=25`, `content=null`, `reasoning_tokens=0`.
After: `completion_tokens=159`, `reasoning_tokens=129` (hidden), `content='{"location": "London", "temperature": 14, "conditions": "Partly cloudy"}'`.

title: [Attention][Kernel] TRITON_MLA_SPARSE: NoPE dim_qk=512 geometry and SM120 support
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

Continues #47629 (a rebase/takeover of #38476), which added the pure-Triton
sparse-MLA path for the 576-wide rope-MLA layout on SM80/SM121. Building on that,
this extends the `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE` backend to the NoPE MLA layout
(`dim_qk=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=0`) used by glm5_next / GLM-5.3-Flash, and marks
SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / Blackwell workstation) as supported.

### What's included

- **NoPE dim_qk=512 geometry**: the kernel derives `BLOCK_DPE` from `dim_qk` at
  dispatch and compile-prunes the RoPE pe load/dot when it's zero, so one kernel
  serves both the 512 (NoPE) and 576 (RoPE) layouts.
- **SM120 support**: `supports_compute_capability` returns True and
  `get_supported_head_sizes` accepts `[512, 576]` on this backend.
- **Indexer fallback**: on archs where DeepGEMM is unavailable (SM80/SM120/SM121)
  the sparse-attention indexer routes its MQA-logits through the Triton fallback
  in `mqa_logits_triton.py`, and the indexer's hard DeepGEMM requirement is
  downgraded to a one-time warning. Without this the indexer can't run at all on
  these archs.
- **bf16-only**: `fp8_ds_mla` still needs the native FlashMLA kernel, so it stays
  out of this backend's supported set; DCP for decode remains gated by the
  existing `NotImplementedError` in the base impl.

### Testing

- New `tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_mla_sparse.py` validates the kernel
  against a naive reference for both geometries (512 and 576) across split counts,
  plus an empty-query NaN-guard case — 18 cases, all pass.
- End-to-end on 4x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) serving GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 with
  `--attention-backend TRITON_MLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16`: coherent
  generation.

`mqa_logits_triton.py` is carried over from #47629 (credited via co-author).

First-time contributor here, so CI won't run until a maintainer adds the `ready`
label — happy to address anything.

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2 FP8 on 8×H200 dies with runtime CUDA OOM in sparse_decode_fwd
bodyExcerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

   ## Summary

   On the FlashMLA sparse **fp8 mixed-batch** path, the sparse decode kernel allocates a workspace that
   scales linearly with `--max-num-batched-tokens` and is **not bounded by any workspace limit and not
   accounted for during startup memory profiling**. The server starts fine, serves for days, then dies
   with a runtime `torch.OutOfMemoryError` inside `flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd` the first time a
   batch gets large enough. The OOM kills EngineCore, so every in-flight request fails with
   `EngineDeadError` and the process exits.

   This is not KV-cache pressure: **GPU KV cache usage was 2.0–5.4%** in the minute before the crash,
   with at most 8 concurrent requests.

   The mixed-batch path is selected automatically whenever per-rank head count < 32, i.e. exactly the
   common high-TP configurations. 

   ## Repro

   ```bash
   vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
     --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
     --enable-expert-parallel \
     --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
     --max-model-len 262144 \
     --max-num-seqs 32 \
     --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
     --speculative-config.method mtp \
     --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 5
   # NOTE: --gpu-memory-utilization left at its 0.90 default
   ```

   Then drive mixed prefill+decode traffic until a step fills the token budget. In our case it ran
   ~61 hours before dying during a burst (prompt throughput ~3.6k tok/s, 8 running requests).

title: [Bug][CPU] GLM-5.x (glm_moe_dsa) cannot run on CPU: sparse attention forced by config, no way to disable
bodyExcerpt:
## Environment

- vLLM version: v0.28.0
- Platform: Apple Silicon (M3), macOS 15.7.4, CPU backend
- HF transformers: 5.16.1
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2` (`glm_moe_dsa` / `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`)

## Bug

Any GLM-5.x model (DSA / sparse-attention architecture) fails during engine initialization on the CPU backend:

```
NotImplementedError: Sparse Attention is not supported on CPU.
  File "vllm/platforms/cpu.py", line 89, in get_attn_backend_cls
    raise NotImplementedError("Sparse Attention is not supported on CPU.")
```

This makes GLM-5.2 unusable on CPU even for functional verification / CI, and there is **no user-facing way to disable sparse attention**.

## Root cause

Sparse attention is enabled implicitly by a `hasattr` check in the model code, while the config class always injects the trigger attribute:

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py:1080` and `:1373`:
   ```python
   self.is_v32 = hasattr(config, "index_topk")
   ```
   → `is_v32=True` → sparse MLA path → CPU raises `NotImplementedError`.

2. The trigger attribute can never be removed by the user: `GlmMoeDsaConfig.__init__` (transformers 5.16.1, `configuration_glm_moe_dsa.py:125`) hard-codes it as a default parameter:
   ```python
   index_topk: int = 2048
   ```
   Even if `index_topk` is deleted from `config.json`, the loaded config object always has the attribute (verified: `hasattr(config, "index_topk")` is `True` after removing it from the JSON).

So there is no config-level workaround: sparse attention is architecturally forced for DSA models on every platform, and the CPU platform has no sparse support (no kernels, and the sparse indexer/top-k machinery is GPU-oriented).

## Reproduction

With only the model config (dummy weights, no weight download needed):

```bash
# fetch config.json + tokenizer only, e.g. into models/GLM-5.2
vllm bench latency --model models/GLM-5.2 --load-format dummy \
  --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --max-model-len 4096

title: Bugfix: use PCP slot mappings for PIECEWISE capture
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- build PIECEWISE capture slot mappings through `PCPManager` so dummy attention metadata follows the rank-major PCP layout
- cover the PCP2 mixed-batch capture shape with a focused regression test
- run both PCP GSM8K end-to-end configurations with PIECEWISE CUDA graphs

## Root cause

PIECEWISE capture created a global dummy slot mapping with `num_tokens` entries. **The PCP with `TRITON_MLA` preparation path consumes a rank-major mapping with `pcp_size * num_tokens` entries**, so mixed capture batches could fail while reshaping the mapping.

For example, the 56-token capture case with PCP2 enters `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs()` with only 56 slot-mapping entries and fails at:

```text
gathered_slot_mapping.view(pcp_size, local_num_tokens)
RuntimeError: shape '[2, 56]' is invalid for input of size 56
```

## Why the previous PCP PIECEWISE validation did not expose it

The regression coverage added by #53515 exercised PCP batch preparation and dispatch, but did not run the CUDA graph capture input preparation in `ModelCudaGraphManager.prepare_inputs_to_capture()`.

The end-to-end H20 validation also selected `FLASH_ATTN_MLA`. Its dummy capture batch was classified as pure decode, so the PCP cache-update path returned before the rank-major prefill reshape and masked the undersized mapping. Backends that classify the same dummy batch as mixed prefill/decode reach the reshape and expose the failure.

## Cross-GPU reproduction

H100 controlled A/B configuration: GLM-4.7-Flash, TP1 + PCP2 + EP, `max_num_seqs=32`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, and PIECEWISE CUDA graphs.

| GPU | Attention backend | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | auto-selected `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` | all 11 capture sizes completed and the service became healthy |
| H100 | forced `TRITON_MLA` | reproduced `shape '[2, 56]' is invalid for input of size 56` during the first graph-memory profiling capture |
| RTX 5090 | auto-selected `TRITON_MLA` with DSV2LiteChat |

title: [Feature] Add PCP O-Proj tensor parallelism
bodyExcerpt:
This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-pcp-o-proj-tp` path that shards the resident MLA O-Proj parameter across the combined PCP-by-TP rank grid while preserving the existing TP reduction semantics.

## Summary

The feature further partitions each TP-local O-Proj input shard across the PCP group, reducing the resident O-Proj parameter on each rank to `1 / PCP` of its standard TP layout. The MVP is intentionally limited to `decode_context_parallel_size=1` and eager execution.

Supported architectures are DeepSeek V2, V3, and V3.2, plus GLM-4 MoE Lite MLA. Supported O-Proj representations are `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 with a CUTLASS-compatible post-load layout. The NVFP4 adapter is an implementation example for quantized methods; its packed weight and swizzled block scale are handled explicitly. Other post-load layouts fail during post-load processing.

## Runtime behavior

The model runner records the logical, pre-partition batch type and propagates it consistently to every PCP rank. This keeps the collective decision identical even when PCP token partitioning gives different local batch shapes to different ranks.

- For prefill or mixed batches, generic MLA starts an asynchronous O-Proj weight all-gather after Q/KV normalization and before the remaining Q projection, RoPE, indexer, and main attention work. O-Proj waits for the gather only when the full TP shard is needed, then runs the normal TP-local O-Proj computation.
- For decode-only batches, each rank slices the TP attention output to its local PCP feature shard, computes a partial O-Proj result with the resident weight, and all-reduces that result over PCP.
- The existing TP reduction behavior remains unchanged, including paths where TP reduction is handled outside O-Proj.

## Implementation

- Adds a reusable `TPWeightSwitchMixin` with opt-in tensor/method specifications, asynchronous gather and wait handling, local/full tensor alias switching, and representation-specific prepare/finalize h

title: fix(parser): attach structural tag when parsers share an engine
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Fixes #53745. When the reasoning parser and the tool parser resolve to the same streaming parser engine (for example `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`), vLLM attached no xgrammar structural tag, so strict tool calling was silently a no-op.

## Root cause

`ParserManager.get_parser` short-circuits when both parser names map to the same `ParserEngine` subclass and returns the raw engine class. That engine's `tool_parser_cls` is the generic adapter installed by `make_adapters()`, which does not carry `structural_tag_model`. Only the registered tool parser (for example `Qwen3EngineToolParser`) carries it. `ParserEngine.adjust_request` only sets `skip_special_tokens` and never applies the structural tag, which lives on `DelegatingParser._apply_structural_tag`.

Net effect: with a shared engine pair, `strict: true`, `tool_choice="required"`, and `VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING` all produced unconstrained tool-call arguments, so a model misfire on a parameter name reached the client as malformed keys instead of being caught by the grammar.

## Fix

Keep the single-engine fast path, but:

- `ParserManager.get_parser`: when the engine's `tool_parser_cls` is the generic adapter and a more specific registered tool parser exists, preserve the registered one instead of returning the raw engine.
- `ParserEngine.adjust_request`: attach the structural tag for strict or required tool calls, mirroring `DelegatingParser._apply_structural_tag`.

This restores the v0.27.1 behavior for same-engine parser pairs while leaving composed parsers through `DelegatingParser` (for example `deepseek_r1` reasoning with `qwen3_coder` tool) unchanged.

The fix is generic: it also repairs the same latent bug for every other engine-backed pair whose registered tool parser carries a `structural_tag_model` (deepseek_v4, deepseek_v32, glm47_moe, minimax_m2, kimi_k2), not just qwen3.

## Tests

- 2 new tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py`: a monkeypatch

title: BugFix(PCP): use persistent input buffers for PIECEWISE CUDA graphs
bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Fix PIECEWISE CUDA graph execution with PCP by using persistent PCP input buffers during graph capture and sizing graph dispatch from the largest real rank-local PCP batch before padding.

## Implementation

- Decoder graph capture now uses `PCPManager.input_buffers` when PCP is active, ensuring capture and runtime partitioning share persistent `input_ids`, `positions`, and `is_padding` buffers.
- `GPUModelRunner` obtains the graph dispatch size from `PCPManager.get_num_tokens_for_dispatch()`.
- The CUDA graph dispatcher selects the smallest captured token size covering that rank-local maximum.
- The selected `BatchExecutionDescriptor.num_tokens` is passed to PCP partitioning as `padded_num_tokens`, which determines rank-local gather-index and mask capacity.
- A shared `_iter_rank_chunks()` implements rank chunking for both dispatch-size calculation and segment construction.
- PCP raises `ValueError` when `padded_num_tokens` is smaller than the largest rank-local batch.

Representative dispatch mappings:

| Workload | Global tokens | Rank-local maximum | Capture size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PCP2 prefill | 8 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2 prefill | 7 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes | 3 | 3 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes + prefill | 11 | 7 | 8 |
| PCP4, 2 decodes + prefill | 11 | 5 | 8 |

## Validation configuration

- NVIDIA H20 GPUs
- GLM-4.7-Flash
- TP1 + PCP4 + EP4
- `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`
- `max_num_seqs=32`
- `max_model_len=8192`
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80`
- GSM8K 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, maximum output tokens 4096, concurrency 32
- PR head: `1dfcbc289db596b38052c33606a6f32c09d65ee9`
- Validation used the image-aligned FlashMLA Python runtime file; the source changes under test were exactly the PR head.

All four ranks completed 11/11 PIECEWISE graph captures. The service remained healthy after the full run, and logs contained zero graph replay, CUDA error, input-address mismatch, illegal-memory, traceback, engine-dead, initialization-failure signatures.

title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for GLM-5.x/DSV3.2 (Sparse MLA)
bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the GPU tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU).

Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request.

GLM-5.x models using DSV3.2-style sparse MLA should be compatible through FlashInfer's SM100 TRT-LLM sparse-MLA kernel. vLLM currently derives the sparse token-to-request mapping from CPU query boundaries, and the target capability check also includes draft attention that is captured by a separate graph manager. We should wire up the device-length path, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support.

PROPOSED IN https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52783

DEPENDS ON https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808

Parent tracker: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51303

title: [Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark on SM100 sparse MLA
bodyExcerpt: ## Purpose Resolves #52785. This is part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion tracked by #51303. Related GLM-5.2 DSpark bring-up context is in #50851. This enables adaptive DSpark verification with `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend`. It was validated end to end with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` and `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on 4× NVIDIA B300. Before this change, startup failed for two independent reasons: 1. The sparse-MLA metadata builder derived token-to-request mappings from CPU query boundaries. Adaptive verification changes those boundaries on device without synchronizing them back to the CPU. 2. The target graph capability check included the draft model's FlashAttention backend. Draft attention is captured and capability-checked by its own graph manager, and it never consumes the target's adaptive query lengths. ## Changes - Add an SM100 FlashInfer sparse-MLA metadata builder that derives request IDs from device query boundaries and declares variable-length CUDA graph support. - Scope target CUDA graph and query-length compatibility checks to target attention layers while retaining draft groups needed by draft prefill. - Add a real B300 kernel regression using GLM-5.2 dimensions. It compares FlashInfer sparse MLA against SDPA with device query lengths `[1, 7, 3, 5]` and deliberately stale CPU lengths `[4, 4, 4, 4]`. - Add a unit regression proving draft-only groups are excluded without hiding mixed target/draft groups that still participate in target execution. ## Performance Scaled SPEED Bench qualitative sweep, 16K context, 512 output tokens, temperature 1.0, seed 0. The c1 run used 32 prompts, c16 used 128, and the remaining points used 256. Both configurations completed with zero failed requests.

### Proposal to improve performance

At this stage, we are seeking clarification about the semantics and
expected variability of the MTP metrics reported by the vLLM server.
We do not yet have a proposed implementation change.

### Report of performance regression

We have not confirmed a regression between vLLM versions.

All results below were collected with vLLM v0.24.0+cu129. The aggregate
results of repeated benchmark runs are relatively stable, but the
10-second server-side MTP metrics fluctuate significantly within each run.

Therefore, this report is currently a performance question rather than a
confirmed version-to-version regression.

### Misc discussion on performance

## Description

When serving a local GLM-5.2-FP8 checkpoint with MTP speculative decoding
on 8× NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the server-side `SpecDecoding metrics` reported
every 10 seconds fluctuate significantly within a single benchmark run.

For example, with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, the reported mean acceptance
length changes approximately between 1.0 and 1.7. The per-position
acceptance rates also change significantly between reporting intervals.

We would like to understand whether this is expected because these metrics
are calculated over short reporting windows with changing request/batch
composition, or whether it indicates an issue with MTP, FP8 model
quantization, FP8 KV cache, or scheduling.

title: [ROCm][Quantization] Implement Fp8Config shared-expert FSE compatibility check
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible()` gates AITER fused shared experts (FSE) behind a
quantization compatibility check that currently implements only `QuarkConfig` and
`DeepseekV4FP8Config`. Every other quantization falls through to a catch-all rejection:

```
shared-expert FSE quantization compatibility is not implemented for Fp8Config
```

The practical effect is that models loading with the plain `Fp8Config` accept
`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` and then silently run unfused. There is no error
and no non-zero exit, only one warning per MoE layer per rank buried in startup logs. On
GLM-5.2-FP8 (78 MoE layers, TP8) that is 600+ near-identical warning lines, and it is easy to
believe the flag took effect when it did not.

This PR implements the TODO that sits directly above the catch-all return:

```python
# TODO: Extend FSE support detection to other quantization methods. Typically,
# one would check that the experts and shared_experts use the same
# quantization config.
```

`Fp8Config` carries a single global `weight_block_size` and `activation_scheme` with no
per-layer overrides, so the only source of per-layer variation is `ignored_layers`. Routed and
shared experts therefore share a quantization config exactly when they are either both
quantized or both ignored. Skip status is resolved with `is_layer_skipped()` using the config's
own `packed_modules_mapping` and `ignored_layers_match_mode` — the same call
`Fp8Config.get_quant_method()` makes — so the check asks the quantization layer the question it
already asks itself rather than inventing a parallel rule.

The branch fails closed: any asymmetry between the routed and shared experts returns `False`
with a reason mirroring the existing Quark message. It is also restricted to fp8-serialized
checkpoints, since the online-quantization path has not been exercised. It is placed below the

title: [RFC]: Decouple draft-model parallelism from the target model (PCP/DCP + speculative decoding)
bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

vLLM supports context parallelism for the target model (PCP, #25749, and DCP), but speculative decoding currently assumes the drafter uses the same parallel mapping as the target. Two in-flight PRs take different approaches to PCP + MTP:

- #53427 (@pisceskkk) keeps the target PCP-sharded but runs a fully replicated drafter on every PCP rank over the global batch. This is simple and works for any drafter with no PCP awareness, at the cost of repeating long-prefill draft compute and KV writes on every rank.
- #53653 (@GirasoleY) keeps the MTP draft prefill PCP-sharded, restoring global order only at sampling boundaries. This performs better on long prefills and supports the GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA path, but each speculative method needs its own PCP adaptation.

We probably want both eventually:

1. A drafter that hasn't implemented PCP/DCP (ngram, DSpark, EAGLE, suffix decoding, new methods) should still work when the target uses context parallelism, by consuming the global batch.
2. A drafter that has a sharded implementation (MTP today) should run sharded and skip the redundant compute.

The same question comes up for DCP: e.g. Kimi K3 (MLA, so DCP makes sense for the target) paired with a GQA draft model. There it probably makes sense to disable DCP for the draft model, since GQA already shards KV heads across TP and DCP would just add latency.

We already let the draft model diverge from the target config in some places: `draft_tensor_parallel_size` (draft TP=1 under target TP=N), and the per-draft `moe_backend` / `attention_backend` overrides in `SpeculativeConfig`. This RFC proposes generalizing that into a separate drafter parallel config so we don't accumulate ad-hoc per-method special cases in the model runner.

## Proposed Change

Give the draft model its own parallel config instead of implicitly inheriting the target's: `SpeculativeConfig` grows a `draft_parallel_config` (subsuming the existing `draft_tensor_parallel_size` field), where each para

title: [PCP][Spec Decode] Support MTP speculative decoding with PCP
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Stacked on #53660 (review only the top commit). Enables MTP speculative decoding in the MRV2 GPU runner when prefill context parallelism is enabled.

The target model stays PCP-sharded; the MTP drafter runs replicated over the global batch on every PCP rank. Because #53660 makes the drafter build its own step-0 attention metadata from the input batch — which is the restored *global* batch by the time `propose()` runs — no PCP-specific metadata plumbing is needed at all. The remaining diff is:

- `DraftModelSpeculator` clears `prefill_context_parallel_size` in its config copy so the drafter's attention groups, forward context, and cudagraphs are built without PCP.
- `PCPManager.partition_batch` supports multi-token decode rows: reuses the GPU request-state positions verbatim (the CPU `num_computed_tokens` is only an async upper bound after speculative rejection), derives local `seq_lens` from segment end positions, and takes last-token logits indices directly instead of recombining sampled/draft tokens (local logits are never sampled; the global batch already materialized draft tokens).
- `restore_hidden_states` appends explicit zero rows when the global batch is graph-padded (PIECEWISE capture sizes), and `restore_hidden_state_buffer` restores persistent max-token buffers (DeepSeek V4's pre-hc_head residual) by slicing to the rank-local padded token count first.
- Config validation rejects the unsupported combinations: non-MTP methods, sparse MLA, DCP, adaptive verification.

This is the minimal-diff replacement for #53427, coordinated as the outcome of reviewing that PR: the partitioning/restore logic here is adapted from it (credited via `Co-authored-by: QiuChunshuo`), while its metadata plumbing (`_maybe_prepare_replicated_pcp_attn`, the `_build_draft_attn_metadata` signature widening, and two model-runner call sites) is superseded by #53660. #53427's GSM8K validation (GLM-4.7-Flash, PCP4, MTP3: acceptance rate/length matchi

title: [XPU] Fix sparse-MLA metadata sync
bodyExcerpt:
Fix issue below for sparse-MLA FP8 MoE models (e.g. GLM-5.2, DeepSeek DSA) on Intel GPUs. 
Sparse-MLA metadata sync (xpu_mla_sparse.py): The shared MLA layer (mla_attention.py::forward_impl) unconditionally reads num_decodes/num_prefills/num_decode_tokens on every MLA metadata; the CUDA sparse backends carry them via SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder, but the XPU sparse backend built its own metadata without them, so a sparse-MLA run on XPU crashed with "'XPUMLASparseMetadata' object has no attribute 'num_decode_tokens'". Add the fields and populate them so all tokens route through the top-k sparse MQA path (num_decode_tokens == num_actual_tokens, num_prefills == 0), which this backend already implements for both prefill and decode; this keeps num_mha_tokens at 0 and avoids the dense-MHA prefill branch (whose prefill-only fields this backend does not provide).

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Handle sparse MLA metadata after DCP Manager refactor
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

DCP Manager refactoring #50484 is focused on DCP for dense MLA, which does not handle sparse MLA properly.

- `MLASparseMetadata` does not inherit `MLACommonMetadata`, thus `attn_metadata.decode` attribute access should be guarded by getattr
- DCP query-gather assumes a decode query, so its workspace (direct_dcp_q_gather_workspace) is too small for prefill queries (which is passed via forced MQA codepath).
- Forced MQA codepath must be considered in DCP Manager combine as well.

Note that the two sparse MLA backend (flashinfer_mla_sparse, flashmla_sparse) shares the same codepath and thus this PR covers both.

## Test Plan

vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \

  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45
